task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 2 (design-level, from REVIEWER not CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR this time): REVIEWER FAILed Step 2d on OQ-5 (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02d-reviewer.json) -- read its result.summary in full for the complete reasoning, it is thorough and you should not re-litigate it, only implement the resolution. Ruling: M6's insert-if-absent creation of an instance_projections row (default ACTIVE status) on an instance's first append oversteps into EE-01/S3's 'meaningful population at instance-start' territory that REQ-023 explicitly defers. Evidence REVIEWER cited: REQ-025's own AC text says 'update' only for instance_projections (unlike instance_sequence's explicit insert-if-absent callout); InstanceProjection is the only event-store schema module REQ-023 gave an update_changeset/2, which M6's current design bypasses; 'at instance start' population is explicitly named as EE-01/S3's job.

Required redesign: rewrite Section 6's M1 and M6 (and Section 9's OQ-5, now resolved not open) in lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md: (1) M1 (active-instance guard) -- when no instance_projections row exists for the target instance_id, return a distinct error (e.g. {:error, :instance_not_started}) instead of treating this as 'implicitly active/new'. Only CANCELLED/COMPLETED-status existing rows produce :instance_terminated; a missing row is a *different* error case, not folded into the terminal-instance path. (2) M6 (instance_projections update) -- becomes update-only, using InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2 (the tool REQ-023 built for exactly this), never insert_changeset/2 or on_conflict:-based upsert. This means append/2 can only succeed against an instance that already has an instance_projections row (created by some future EE-01/S3 mechanism, or directly by a test fixture's own Repo.insert -- REVIEWER explicitly confirmed test fixtures seeding the row directly, bypassing append(), is the correct test strategy and does not undermine coverage). (3) Update the error taxonomy in Section 5 to add :instance_not_started (or your chosen name) as a distinct append_error() case, and update Section 11's acceptance-criteria traceability table to reflect that AC1's terminated-instance test and AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6's tests all pre-seed an instance_projections row via direct Repo.insert rather than relying on append/2 to create one. State explicitly in Section 9 that OQ-5 is now RESOLVED per REVIEWER's Step 2d ruling, not still open. Keep everything else in the design (tenant_id derivation, error taxonomy for other cases, M2-M5) unchanged -- this is a targeted revision to M1/M6/OQ-5, not a full rewrite. REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed the first draft (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-01b-code-design-validator.json) on the 'no implementation code present' check -- Section 6 (6.1 P5/P6, 6.2.2-6.2.6 M2-M6, 6.3) contained near-literal, copy-pasteable Elixir/Ecto code: real with/case/do/else syntax, real Ecto.Multi/Ecto.Query/Ecto.Repo calls (repo.insert/2, from(...) |> repo.one/2, repo.update_all/3), real option keywords (on_conflict:, conflict_target:, prefix:, lock:), real map/struct literals, and append/2's full real implementation body -- not algorithm-shape prose. Rewrite Section 6 entirely in the SAME style as your own req024-event-type-registry.md Section 4.4 (already validator-approved): English-prose conditionals describing what each step does and checks, naming the operation (e.g. 'lock instance_sequence's row FOR UPDATE, or insert it if absent') without writing the actual Ecto/Elixir syntax that performs it. Keep every other section (the design decisions, the error taxonomy, tenant_id derivation via a named reversing function, OQ-1/OQ-5) -- those passed validation and do not need to change; do not re-litigate them, only convert Section 6 from code to prose algorithm steps. Design lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md for REQ-025 (Event append). This is Letflow's first multi-table atomic transaction (Ecto.Multi across events/instance_sequence/instance_projections/idempotency-sidecar/event_payload_store) and first requirement needing tenant_id derived from the Ecto :prefix rather than accepted as a caller argument -- both need concrete, unambiguous design, not left to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment. Specify: the exact Ecto.Multi step order and each step's operation; the locking mechanism for instance_sequence (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE-equivalent in Ecto, exact query shape, described in prose not code); the full StoreError-equivalent tagged-tuple/exception error set (one distinct, pattern-matchable case per named failure mode in the requirement text); how tenant_id is derived from :prefix by reversing schema_name_for_tenant/1 (name the reversing function and its signature); the metadata pre-transaction validation (>50 entries, key/value length limits, non-string values) and confirm it runs before the transaction opens, not inside it. Branch feature/WF02-REQ025-20260817 already exists and is checked out.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 2 applied, resolving REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-02d-reviewer.json). Four targeted edits to lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md, nothing else touched: (1) Section 5.3's append_error() gained a distinct {:error, :instance_not_started} case, documented as reachable only when no instance_projections row exists yet, textually separated from {:error, {:instance_terminated, status}} which now explicitly only fires when a row DOES exist and is terminal. (2) Section 6.2.1 (M1, active-instance guard): 'no row found' branch changed from 'succeed, recording :new_instance' to 'fail the step with {:error, :instance_not_started}' -- append/2 can no longer originate a new instance's projection row; M6 is unreachable on this path since M1 aborts the whole Multi first. (3) Section 6.2.6 (M6) rewritten from a genuine insert-if-absent-else-update UPSERT (using InstanceProjection.insert_changeset/2 + on_conflict:, explicitly avoiding update_changeset/2) to update-only, using InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2 -- the changeset REQ-023 built for exactly this -- keyed on an instance_id M1 already guarantees exists and is non-terminal; no more 'row does not yet exist -> create it' branch. (4) Section 9's OQ-5 entry rewritten from an open judgment call to 'RESOLVED per REVIEWER's Step 2d ruling', restating REVIEWER's four-point evidence (AC-text asymmetry between instance_sequence and instance_projections, InstanceProjection being the only schema module with update_changeset/2, 'at instance start' naming EE-01/S3 explicitly, and the design's own prior counter-argument not holding up) and the resolution now built into M1/M6. Two secondary edits kept the rest of the doc consistent with the above rather than leaving stale statements behind: Section 10's cross-module-dependency table entry for the five schema modules (previously stated 'InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2 is deliberately NOT used') now states it IS used for M6, and Section 11's acceptance-criteria traceability table gained a note that every AC1-AC6 test must pre-seed the target instance's instance_projections row via a direct Repo.insert in test setup (REVIEWER-confirmed strategy) since append/2 itself can no longer create one. Verified via grep across the full file for every remaining 'new_instance'/'insert-if-absent ... instance_projections'/'create the row'/'create it' mention post-edit: the three surviving hits (lines ~306, ~495, ~852) all correctly refer to the future EE-01/S3 mechanism or a test fixture's own Repo.insert as the thing that creates the row, never append/2 itself -- no contradictory statement left anywhere in the document. Sections/content NOT touched, per the rework instruction's explicit 'targeted revision, not a full rewrite' scope: tenant_id derivation (Section 4), M2-M5 (Sections 6.2.2-6.2.5), OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-3/OQ-4/OQ-6 (Section 9), invariants (Section 8).
